question.text: What will be Mexico's forecasted meat consumption for 2027?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the forecasted combined domestic consumption of meat (beef and veal, chicken, and swine) for Mexico in 2027 (measured in 1,000 metric tonnes carcass-weight equivalent), according to USDA Foreign Agricultural Service's [market and trade data](https://apps.fas.usda.gov/psdonline/app/index.html#/app/advQuery).
question.fine_print:
To get the resolution value:

* Select all of "Meat, Beaf and Veal", "Meat, Chicken", and "Meat, Swine" from *Commodities*
* Click *Summarize* below
* Select "Domestic Consumption" from *Attributes*
* Select "Mexico" from *Countries*
* Select "2027" from *Market Years*
* Click *Run Query*

The question will resolve according to the first available forecast for 2027.

If the USDA Foreign Agricultural Service ceases to record data on Mexico's forecasted meat consumption, another suitable credible source may be used to resolve this question.

# Mexico's 2027 meat consumption forecast (USDA FAS): research notes

**Bottom line:** USDA probably already published its first 2027 forecast for Mexico in the PSD database around October 9, 2026, alongside its October circular. If so, the question is effectively settled, but I could not read the number. The PSD query app runs on JavaScript, the circular and GAIN reports came back as unreadable binary PDFs, and the fas.usda.gov report pages returned 403 errors. The pieces I could find point to a total of about 10.8 million tonnes (calculation in section 4).

## 1. Resolution source
- PSD Online is a JavaScript app, so I could not run the query myself. [PSD](https://apps.fas.usda.gov/psdonline/app/index.html#/app/advQuery)
- 2026-10-09 (the PDF's creation date): the October 2026 "Livestock and Poultry: World Markets and Trade" circular includes 2027 forecasts. The October edition is normally the first to carry next-year numbers, and PSD is updated at the same time. [circular](https://apps.fas.usda.gov/psdonline/circulars/livestock_poultry.pdf)
- A search snippet of that circular shows a Mexico "Total Dom. Consumption" row running from 2,538 to 3,005 (thousand tonnes). 2,538 matches the 2022 pork value in the question's table, so 3,005 is likely the 2027 pork forecast. I could not confirm the year labels. [circular](https://apps.fas.usda.gov/psdonline/circulars/livestock_poultry.pdf)

## 2. Current status
- The first 2027 forecast very likely already exists in PSD (since about October 9, 2026), which would nearly settle the question. I could not see the beef or chicken values, or verify the pork value.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-04: Mexico's government is reviewing its 2027 rules for zero-tariff beef and pork import quotas (the PACIC anti-inflation package). The screwworm outbreak has left a surplus of cattle at home. [El Imparcial](https://www.elimparcial.com/dinero/2026/11/04/ante-la-sobreoferta-interna-provocada-por-el-gusano-barrenador-y-la-persistente-necesidad-de-importacion-de-carne-el-gobierno-de-claudia-sheinbaum-busca-redefinir-el-mercado-para-blindar-el-poder-adquisitivo-del-consumidor-frente-a-las-demandas-de-la-industria/)
- 2026-11-02: the Mexican Meat Council (CoMeCarne) expects national meat consumption to grow 3.5% in 2027. For January to August 2026 versus a year earlier, it reports chicken up 3%, pork up 2.9% and beef down 2.5%. The beef/pork and chicken import schemes end December 31, 2026. Its 2025 total of 11,271 thousand tonnes uses a different method from USDA's. [Publimetro](https://www.publimetro.com.mx/noticias/2026/11/02/mexico-desabasto-de-carne-precios-importaciones-2027/)
- 2026-10-14: coverage of USDA's October report says Mexico's 2027 beef exports rise 7.5% and pork exports rise 9.1% to 240,000 tonnes. Another snippet says Mexico's beef imports are forecast 5% lower in 2027 as import demand weakens. [Meatingplace](https://meatingplace.com/daily-livestock-report-usda-forecasts-higher-global-chicken-production-flat-beef-and-pork-markets/)
- 2026-09: USDA's economic outlook (ERS) says Mexican pork imports are forecast to rise in both 2026 and 2027. [ERS LDP-M-387](https://www.ers.usda.gov/media/29662/ldp-m-387.pdf?v=54460)
- 2026-08-24: the USDA Mexico City office's annual livestock report (GAIN MX2026-0040) forecasts flat beef production in 2027 and a 3% rise in commercial pig slaughter. [GAIN page](https://www.fas.usda.gov/data/gain/2026/08/mexico-livestock-and-products-annual)
- 2026-08-17: per the poultry annual (MX2026-0041), 2027 chicken consumption is 5.5 million tonnes (up 3%), production 4.4 (up 2%) and imports 1.1 (up 4%). This is the attaché's own estimate, not the official USDA figure. [enAlimentos](https://enalimentos.lat/noticias/13010-produccion-de-pollo-en-mexico-crecera-2-en-2027-usda.html)

## 4. Base rates
- USDA PSD totals from the question's table (thousand tonnes): 8,471 (2020), 8,826, 9,147, 9,544, 9,850, 10,185, 10,601 (2026).
- Yearly increases: +355, +321, +397, +306, +335, +416. The average is about +355 (+3.5 to 4.2%), and the total rose every year.
- Plain arithmetic, not a forecast:
  - Last increase applied to 2026: 10,601 + ~355 ≈ 10,950.
  - Component pieces: chicken about 5,500 (attaché) + pork 3,005 (unverified) + beef near its 2026 level of 2,320 ≈ 10,800.
- Beef is the weak component. Production is flat, imports are forecast down 5%, exports up and January to August consumption down 2.5%.
- Official numbers often differ from the attaché's figures by tens of thousands of tonnes.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market on this question. The markets provided (Mexico GDP, tariffs, Banxico, elections) don't match it.
- Expert views:
  - CoMeCarne: +3.5% in 2027.
  - USDA long-term projections: per-person consumption keeps rising toward 82.5 kg by 2033. [ERS](https://www.ers.usda.gov/amber-waves/2024/august/meat-consumption-in-mexico-led-by-poultry-will-continue-rising-over-next-decade-usda-projections-show)
  - Private forecasters expect Mexico's GDP to grow about 1.83 to 1.86% in 2027 (Banxico October survey). [La Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/2026/11/04/economia/021n1eco)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Monthly WASDE reports and PSD updates: November 10 and December 2026, then January, February, March and April 2027. These could revise the numbers, but the question resolves on the first 2027 forecast, which was probably the October 2026 release.
- Mexico's decision on 2027 import quotas and tariffs (by December 31, 2026).
- Phased reopening of US imports of Mexican cattle (started August 2026), which affects beef supply in Mexico.
- Possible US tariffs on Mexican goods on January 1, 2027 (Kalshi gives 83% to a rate of 10% or more).
- USDA Mexico semi-annual reports (about February to March 2027) and the April 2027 circular.

**Recommendation:** run the PSD query linked in the question directly. If it shows 2027 values dated October 2026, that is very likely the resolution value.

# Mexico 2027 meat consumption (USDA PSD): research brief

**In short:** USDA's first official 2027 forecast for Mexico has already been published. It came out on 2026-10-09 in the "Livestock and Poultry: World Markets and Trade" report, so the resolution value most likely already exists in PSD Online. I could not read that value directly. The report's PDF would not parse, and the PSD query tool needs JavaScript. What I could confirm is the official pork forecast, plus partial clues for beef and chicken.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-10-09: The USDA FAS report (23 pages, PDF metadata dated 2026-10-09) contains 2027 forecasts for each country. I could not extract its tables. [FAS circular](https://apps.fas.usda.gov/psdonline/circulars/livestock_poultry.pdf)
- 2026-10-13/23: Pork figures for Mexico in 2027, as quoted from that report: production 1.49 MMT (+3.1%), imports 1.76 MMT (+3.5%), exports 240,000 t (+9.1%). Production plus imports minus exports gives about 3,010 thousand tonnes consumed, assuming stocks barely change. That figure is my arithmetic, not a published number. [3tres3](https://www.3tres3.com/es-mx/ultima-hora/porcicultura-mundial-primeras-estimaciones-del-usda-para-2027_17781/)
- 2026-10-22: Beef: the same report projects Mexican beef production rising in 2027. Search snippets of the report say Mexico's beef imports are forecast 5% lower in 2027, but I could not verify this in the PDF. [Beef Magazine](https://www.beefmagazine.com/market-news/global-beef-trade-update)
- 2026-10-15: Beef: Mexico's exports are forecast up about 30,000 t (+8%). [APEA](https://www.apea.org.ar/para-2027-habra-menos-produccion-mundial-y-menos-exportaciones-de-carne/)
- I found no official October numbers for Mexico's 2027 beef or chicken consumption.

## 2. Current status
- The first forecast already exists, as of 2026-10-09. The open questions are its exact value and whether resolution will use that first figure or a later revision (USDA updates these in January and April). The question says "first available forecast", which points to the October 2026 figure.
- Other forecasts for 2027:
  - 2026-08: The USDA attaché in Mexico City (a post estimate, not official USDA data) forecasts chicken consumption up 3% to 5.5 MMT in 2027, production up 2% to 4.4 MMT, and imports up 4% to 1.1 MMT. [APEDA copy of GAIN](https://agriexchange.apeda.gov.in/MarketReport/0925904062026821113922831.pdf)
  - 2026-08-24: The attaché's livestock report (MX2026-0040) forecasts flat beef production in 2027, and a 3% rise in commercial hog slaughter. [FAS GAIN](https://www.fas.usda.gov/data/gain/2026/08/mexico-livestock-and-products-annual)
- Adding pork (about 3,010), chicken (about 5,450 to 5,500) and beef (about 2,300 to 2,350, if consumption is near the 2026 level of 2,320) gives roughly 10,750 to 10,850. This rests on partly unverified pieces, so treat it as unconfirmed.

## 3. Recent news
- 2026-11-04: Mexico's government is reviewing the 2027 rules for zero-tariff beef and pork import quotas under its anti-inflation package (PACIC). Ranchers and meat processors disagree, and the screwworm outbreak has left a domestic cattle surplus. [El Imparcial](https://www.elimparcial.com/dinero/2026/11/04/ante-la-sobreoferta-interna-provocada-por-el-gusano-barrenador-y-la-persistente-necesidad-de-importacion-de-carne-el-gobierno-de-claudia-sheinbaum-busca-redefinir-el-mercado-para-blindar-el-poder-adquisitivo-del-consumidor-frente-a-las-demandas-de-la-industria/)
- 2026-11-02: CoMeCarne, the Mexican meat council, warns that import permits and the zero-tariff schemes expire on 2026-12-31.
  - It expects national meat consumption to grow 3.5% in 2027.
  - From January to August 2026, chicken consumption rose 3%, pork 2.9%, and beef fell 2.5%.
  - CoMeCarne's own figures are much higher than USDA's (for example, pork at 3.75 MMT in 2025). [Publimetro](https://www.publimetro.com.mx/noticias/2026/11/02/mexico-desabasto-de-carne-precios-importaciones-2027/)
- 2026-11-03: Rabobank reports weak North American pork demand in Q3 2026. [National Hog Farmer](https://www.nationalhogfarmer.com/market-news/soft-demand-export-volatility-cloud-2027-global-pork-outlook)
- 2026-10-26: The US-Mexico border partly reopened to cattle in August and September 2026, which could reduce Mexico's domestic beef supply. [farmdoc daily](https://farmdocdaily.illinois.edu/2026/10/us-mexico-cattle-trade-and-beef-markets.html)
- 2026-11-04: Mexico's GDP grew 3.2% year on year in Q3 2026. Private-sector economists forecast about 1.8% growth for 2027. [Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/2026/11/04/economia/021n1eco)

## 4. Base rates
- Year-on-year changes in the totals from the question's table: +355 (2021), +321, +397, +306, +335, +416 (2026). The average is about +355 per year (about 3.6%), and every year rose.
- Adding the average to the 2026 total of 10,601 gives about 10,956. Adding the smallest and largest increases gives 10,907 to 11,017. These are simple extrapolations, not forecasts.
- USDA's first forecast for the coming year tends to differ from later estimates by tens of thousands of tonnes per commodity. The 2026 figures in the table may themselves have been revised in October.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on this question. The markets collected (Mexico GDP, tariffs, Banxico, elections) are only loosely related.
- Expert views:
  - The attaché expects chicken at 5.5 MMT.
  - CoMeCarne expects total consumption up 3.5% in 2027.
  - USDA's long-term projections (made in 2024, running to 2033) see continued per-person growth, led by poultry. [ERS](https://www.ers.usda.gov/amber-waves/2024/august/meat-consumption-in-mexico-led-by-poultry-will-continue-rising-over-next-decade-usda-projections-show)

## 6. Upcoming events
- About 2026-12-10: the December WASDE report (usually small changes to foreign meat figures).
- By 2026-12-31: Mexico decides on 2027 import quotas and tariffs, while the zero-tariff schemes expire.
- About 2027-01-12: the January Livestock and Poultry: World Markets and Trade report, with revisions.
- Around February to March 2027: the attaché's semi-annual livestock and poultry reports for Mexico.
- About 2027-04-09: the April World Markets and Trade report, the last revision before the question resolves (around 2027-05-01).
- Also: the pace of cattle exports to the US as the border reopens, screwworm developments, and US tariffs on Mexico (Kalshi puts 83% on a rate of 10% or more on 2027-01-01).

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** The question resolves on the first published 2027 forecast. That was very likely released in PSD around October 9, 2026, alongside the October circular. Formal resolution is about 2027-05-01.

(b) **Latest known value:** The 2026 forecast is 10,601 thousand MT. It comes from the question's table and may have been revised since. A circular snippet suggests 2027 pork is about 3,005, but I could not verify this.

(c) **If nothing changed:** About 10,601.

(d) **If the trend continued:** The average annual increase is about +355, giving roughly 10,950. A component build gives a lower figure:
- Chicken about 5,450 to 5,500 (the attaché's 5.5 million, adjusted)
- Pork about 3,005
- Beef about 2,250 to 2,320 (flat production, imports down 5%, exports up, consumption year to date down 2.5%)

This sums to about 10,750 to 10,800.

(e) **Historical variation:** Annual changes ranged from +306 to +416, so roughly ±60 around the trend. Uncertainty here also comes from the unverified pork figure and from the gap between attaché and official estimates, which is often tens of thousands of tonnes.

(f) **Experts:**
- CoMeCarne expects +3.5%, which would give about 10,970 on the USDA base.
- The attaché's chicken figure is 5.5 million.
- The USDA long-term projections show continued growth.
- No prediction market covers this question.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- Low: USDA cut beef sharply because of the screwworm outbreak and trade disruption, revised the 2026 base down, and set chicken near 5,400. The total would be about 10,450.
- High: the official chicken figure is 5,550 or more, beef holds at 2,350 and pork about 3,060. The total would be about 11,000 or more.
